verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents point-in-time recovery and a time-travel feature that restores the database to an earlier point, which covers recovering from accidental drops. There is no evidence of read-only querying of data as of a past timestamp; the documented time travel is a restore operation, not an as-of query. missing for 10: querying data as of a past point without restoring, documented per-table restore granularity, hands-on or independent corroboration of recovery.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can time-travel — query data as of a past point and restore dropped or corrupted tables from history

citations.quote: Point-in-time recovery rolls you back to any moment, so an accidental drop is a quick cleanup, not an incident.
Time travel restores the database to an earlier point, backed by object-storage durability for the data.
Automated daily backups, the recovery model, and why there is no manual BACKUP/RESTORE.
